correctness.rationale: All \(n_j\) are positive, with \(r\ge2\) and \(N\ge2\). The transition \(P\) splits into a zero part and an invertible \(r\)-dimensional quotient \(Q\) (determinant \((-1)^r(1-r)\prod_jd_j\)). The zero spectral mass is exactly \(1-1/a\) and identifies the root part. The explicitly inverted diagonal quotient resolvent has strictly separated negative poles \(-s/(N-s)\), each with positive residue \(m_s\,s/(N-s)\); this uniquely recovers all other part sizes for known \(N\). The finite \(2N\)-moment cutoff follows from the spectral theorem and an at-most-\(2N\)-support Vandermonde argument. The complete bipartite boundary is exact. Standalone rational code checks 25,856 equalities through \(N=11\); no finite check is taken as proof for all \(N\).

value.rationale: A complete infinite class of graphs can be identified from the return law at one vertex, with a constructive pole-residue decoder and a uniform finite observation horizon once order is known.
